security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting, read-oriented Azure documentation examples, and normal Azure Monitor SDK configuration. No prompt injection, covert exfiltration intent, destructive command guidance, or automatic network behavior was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples triggered shell-execution detectors.
remediation.suggestion: Label command blocks as examples and keep placeholders explicit so installers do not interpret them as automatic execution steps.

remediation.issue: The TypeScript quick start references an Application Insights connection string environment variable.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note telling users to store connection strings securely and avoid printing them in logs or prompts.

content.user_title: Monitor Azure Apps with Observability References
content.value_statement: Azure teams need quick guidance for metrics, traces, logs, alerts, and workbook workflows. This skill organizes Azure Monitor, Application Insights, Log Analytics, KQL, and SDK references for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users.
actual_capabilities: Map Azure observability tasks to Azure Monitor, Application Insights, Log Analytics, alerts, and workbooks.
Reference Azure MCP tool names for metrics queries, log queries, Kusto queries, and Application Insights resource listing.
Provide Azure CLI examples for listing workspaces, querying logs, listing alerts, and reading metrics.
Offer KQL examples for recent exceptions, request performance, and Azure resource usage.
Summarize SDK setup guidance for OpenTelemetry, Monitor Query, Log Ingestion, and Application Insights management.
limitations: It is a documentation skill and does not include executable automation scripts.
It assumes Azure credentials, subscriptions, and any MCP server configuration are already handled by the user.
It provides condensed SDK guidance and points to separate skills for deeper framework-specific patterns.
It does not create alerts, dashboards, workbooks, or Azure resources by itself.

use_cases.title: Investigate production telemetry
use_cases.description: Find the right Azure service, query pattern, and metric source for errors, latency, or infrastructure symptoms.

use_cases.title: Add application instrumentation
use_cases.description: Use OpenTelemetry and Application Insights references to plan basic tracing, logging, and sampling setup.

use_cases.title: Prepare operational reporting
use_cases.description: Choose Log Analytics, KQL, alerts, and workbooks guidance for incident reviews and service health reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Azure observability service
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose between Azure Monitor, Application Insights, Log Analytics, alerts, and workbooks for this monitoring task: [describe task].

prompt_templates.title: Draft a KQL investigation query
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a KQL query for Log Analytics that investigates [error, latency, or resource symptom] over [time range]. Explain which table and fields to review.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Application Insights instrumentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my application stack: [language and framework]. Recommend Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry or Application Insights setup steps, sampling guidance, and secure configuration practices.

prompt_templates.title: Design an incident observability workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Azure observability workflow for [service name]. Include metrics, traces, logs, KQL queries, alerts, workbook views, and SDK references for ongoing operations.

output_examples.input: Which Azure service should I use to investigate slow API requests?
output_examples.output: Use Application Insights for request duration and dependency traces. Use Log Analytics with KQL when you need deeper correlation across logs, exceptions, and infrastructure data.

output_examples.input: I need a quick query for recent application failures.
output_examples.output: The skill can suggest an AppExceptions query filtered to the last hour, projecting time, message, and stack trace, then sorting by newest events.

output_examples.input: How should I start TypeScript telemetry setup?
output_examples.output: Use the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry package, configure the Azure Monitor exporter options, and keep the Application Insights connection string in a secure environment variable.

best_practices: Confirm the workspace, subscription, and time range before running any telemetry query.
Use projections, aggregations, and limits in KQL to reduce noisy or expensive results.
Store connection strings and credentials outside prompts, logs, and checked-in files.
anti_patterns: Do not paste production secrets or full connection strings into prompts.
Do not run broad log queries without a time filter or row limit.
Do not rely on metrics alone when traces and logs are needed for root cause analysis.

faq.question: Does this skill execute Azure commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides references, example commands, KQL patterns, and SDK guidance for users or agents to apply deliberately.

faq.question: Which Azure services does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure Monitor, Application Insights, Log Analytics, alerts, workbooks, OpenTelemetry, Monitor Query, and Log Ingestion references.

faq.question: Can it help write KQL queries?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes common KQL examples for exceptions, request performance, and resource usage that can be adapted to a workspace.

faq.question: Does it require Azure MCP?
faq.answer: Azure MCP is preferred when available, but the skill also includes Azure CLI and SDK reference material.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production incident response?
faq.answer: It can support investigation planning and query drafting, but users must validate commands, scopes, and results in their Azure environment.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use environment variables, managed identity, Key Vault, or approved secret storage. Do not expose connection strings in prompts or logs.
